Affiliation and AI note: This is promotional editorial from the website whocallme.co.uk, drafted with AI assistance. The code below is an illustrative sketch that was run locally only to confirm it executes. It is not a product, and no real meter numbers were used. The source note The number page for 020 3917 8878 lists a landline, allocation hint Gamma Telecom Holdings Limited, numbering area London. Those labels describe a number range, not a caller. articles.title: "Fixed in the update" is a claim, not evidence: notes on Waymo's freeway recalls and an AI-citation ruling
articles.excerpt: Two things happened on 20 November 2026 that look unrelated. Waymo announced two recalls after its robotaxis drove into closed freeway lanes. And the Kansas Court of Appeals published an opinion about…
articles.body: Two things happened on 20 November 2026 that look unrelated. Waymo announced two recalls after its robotaxis drove into closed freeway lanes. And the Kansas Court of Appeals published an opinion about a self-represented litigant whose AI-drafted filings cited cases that do not exist. A monitoring brief sent to VSO, which maintains the VAP provenance framework, bundled them together and presented provenance logging as the fix for both. We checked the claims against the primary sources and registered both cases (V1111WAYMOFREEWAY and V1120LINGLE). The brief was wrong in a way that is useful for anyone who builds systems that log decisions. Here is what the sources say, and what logging can and cannot do in each case.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.

articles.body: Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago.
